candidates.angle: who takes without giving back is a thief
candidates.evidence: यः भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः (who enjoys, he is indeed a thief)

candidates.angle: the gods give back what humans sacrifice
candidates.evidence: देवाः दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः (radiant beings, nourished by sacrifice, will give)

candidates.evidence: तैर्दत्तान् अप्रदाय (without giving back what is given by them)

angle_en: The thief who takes without giving back
angle_hi: चोर जो बिना लौटाए भोग लेता है

en.intro: Krishna answers a quiet question many people ask: why is sacrifice necessary, and what happens when we stop giving back? Listen to how he answers.
en.notice: The verse turns on a single Sanskrit word, apradaya, which means without giving back. It names the exact moment when a person stops participating in the exchange of life and becomes a thief.
en.next: The next verse draws a sharp line between those who eat the leftovers of sacrifice and those who cook only for themselves.
en.meaning: The radiant beings, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the enjoyments you need. One who enjoys their gifts without offering back is a thief.

hi.intro: कृष्ण एक ऐसे सवाल का जवाब देते हैं जो अक्सर मन में आता है: यज्ञ क्यों ज़रूरी है, और जब हम लौटाना बंद कर देते हैं तो क्या होता है? सुनिए।
hi.meaning: यज्ञ से संतुष्ट हुए देवता तुम्हें इच्छित भोग देते रहेंगे। उनके दिए हुए पदार्थों को उन्हें अर्पित किए बिना जो स्वयं ही भोगता है, वह चोर ही है।
hi.notice: यह पूरा श्लोक एक ही शब्द पर टिका है, अप्रदाय, जिसका अर्थ है बिना लौटाए। यह उस क्षण को दर्शाता है जब मनुष्य जीवन के चक्र में अपनी भागीदारी रोककर चोर बन जाता है।
hi.next: अगला श्लोक उन लोगों के बीच फर्क करता है जो यज्ञ का प्रसाद खाते हैं और केवल अपने लिए पकाते हैं।

en.intro: Krishna answers a quiet question many people ask: why is sacrifice necessary, and what happens when we stop giving back? Listen to how he answers.
en.body: The radiant beings, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the enjoyments you need. One who enjoys their gifts without offering back is a thief. The verse turns on a single Sanskrit word, apradaya, which means without giving back. It names the exact moment when a person stops participating in the exchange of life and becomes a thief. The next verse draws a sharp line between those who eat the leftovers of sacrifice and those who cook only for themselves.

contrast_template: "यह उस क्षण को दर्शाता है जब मनुष्य जीवन के चक्र से बाहर निकलकर चोर बन जाता है।" (The Hindi notice uses the phrase 'बाहर निकलकर' (stepping out/leaving), which creates a contrastive structure implying that by not giving back, one exits the cycle of life to become a thief. The Sanskrit meaning (and the English translation) does not frame this as an 'exiting' or 'leaving' of the cycle, but rather as a failure to participate in the exchange, which is considered theft.)
